entities.name: Per Brahe the Elder
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Per Brahe the Elder (1520–1590) stands as a foundational figure in 16th-century Sweden, instrumental in shaping the early modern state under the Vasa dynasty. As a leading statesman, privy councilor, and later the first Count of Visingsborg, his career spanned the reigns of three kings: Gustav I, Erik XIV, and John III. His influence extended across governance, military affairs, and the consolidation of the Swedish aristocracy, establishing a lineage that would remain prominent for centuries.

Brahe's early career saw him serving King Gustav I, participating in the Dacke War (1542–1543) and later becoming a member of the Privy Council in 1560. Under Erik XIV, he played a crucial role during the Northern Seven Years' War (1563–1570), commanding troops and engaging in diplomatic efforts. His loyalty wavered during Erik XIV's increasingly erratic rule, leading him to support the deposition of Erik in favor of John III in 1568. John III rewarded Brahe significantly, elevating him to the peerage as Count of Visingsborg in 1561, a title and estate that became a powerful symbol of aristocratic landholding and regional governance.

The legacy of Per Brahe the Elder is intrinsically linked to the enduring power and prestige of the Brahe family, who became one of Sweden's wealthiest and most influential noble houses. His administrative acumen and military service helped stabilize the realm during a period of significant internal strife and external conflict, providing a model for later Swedish governance. Through his son, Magnus Brahe, and especially his grandson, Per Brahe the Younger, the family continued to exert immense political, cultural, and intellectual influence, particularly in education and regional development, directly building upon the foundations laid by the Elder.
